elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered still provides that the Agreement "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — renewal is automatic, not by mutual written agreement, and the conditional automatic-renewal elements (30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) are not all satisfied.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — successive one-year (12-month) terms, no multi-year renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires "sixty (60) days written notice" to prevent renewal; to reach preferred the operative text must read thirty (30) days for Customer's non-renewal notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder mechanic appears anywhere in Section 4.1 or the rendered language; a Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date would have to be inserted.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 4.1 contains no renewal price-uplift mechanic and fees are a fixed revenue share under Section 3.1, so no increase is permitted on renewal and the cap is not triggered.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon sixty (60) days written notice to the other" — window computes to exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling; deterministic check "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" ok.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal sentence carries no price-uplift language and no other provision permits an increase on renewal, so no cap is required. (The mapping's supporting quote goes to renewal term rather than pricing, but the substantive absence of an uplift mechanic holds.)

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the sole operative edit reduces the non-renewal notice window from ninety (90) to sixty (60) days, and the price-cap element is untriggered because the Agreement contains no renewal uplift mechanic.

Preferred level is not reached: renewal remains automatic, the opt-out window is 60 rather than 30 days, and no Vendor 60-day pre-renewal reminder obligation exists. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to change "sixty (60) days" to "thirty (30) days" for Customer's non-renewal notice and insert an operative Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date (or convert renewal to mutual written agreement).

Minimal: exactly one numeral is changed within the target sentence; no survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or other extras are added, and favourable existing language (one-year renewal term, either-party notice right, Termination Date definition) is retained verbatim.

Preserves intent: the "Termination Date" definition, the initial one-year term, the anniversary renewal mechanic and the Section 3.1 revenue-share pricing all survive unchanged; no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence is created.

Finding status "deviation" is correct — the original 90-day window failed the fallback ceiling on a material term, so a redline was warranted; note the original was not in walk-away territory (90 days is not longer than 90 days, and renewals are annual, not multi-year).
